To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) dissent is not a major factor in the determination of executive compensation, (ii) it has a modest moderating impact on executive compensation levels, (iii) the moderating impact is restricted to the higher quantiles, and (iv) the moderating effect is stronger in firms with more dispersed shareholding, a higher percentage of independent directors on the board and a higher percentage of institutional ownership.
‘say on pay’, in the sense of shareholders voting on the remunera- tion report, is not an effective mechanism for reducing executive pay levels.
